The maintainer reports that an alpha replacement OS booted on hardware and passed a memory probe; the public build initializes core devices, draws a display test pattern, and parks. Static splash and LED palette changes were separately hardware-confirmed. No GitHub release is listed; the latest source push was 2026-10-13.
projects.summary: Reverse-engineering notes and build tooling for the Analog Rytm MKII OS 1.74, plus a from-source replacement firmware that wraps into a flashable SysEx update. projects.strategy: Static analysis of the OS 1.74 update container and ColdFire firmware, hardware experiments, and an independently built replacement image; also includes reversible static splash/LED data modifications.
projects.subtype: Embedded musical-instrument firmware reverse engineering and replacement
projects.source_available: Public source repository; GitHub metadata reports no repository license. The README explicitly says stock Elektron firmware and raw dumps are not included. Hardware recovery instructions and the restricted scope of the experimental replacement are documented.

projects.strategy: Read device flash, disassemble the dsPIC firmware, reconstruct readable C function-by-function, and cross-reference the source against assembly.
projects.subtype: Embedded power-supply control firmware decompilation and source reconstruction

projects.title: Lelouch (SJCAM SJ4000 Air Allwinner V3 interface replacement)
projects.game: The SJCAM SJ4000 Air camera application and firmware UI behavior on the researched Allwinner V3 board
projects.platform: Specific SJCAM SJ4000 Air board using Allwinner V3, Android 4.4-derived system, ST7789V display, and GC4653 sensor. README says older Novatek NT9665X SJ4000 models use a different firmware and are not covered by Lelouch compatibility.
projects.status: Experimental source project; release v0.0.1 of the Lelouch replacement was published 2026-07-19. The README documents a replacement for the original `sdv` application and build instructions tested on x86-64 Linux. The project does not claim to replace the whole OS or support other SJ4000 board variants.
projects.summary: Reverse-engineering notes, firmware parsers and repackers, protocol research, and Lelouch, a replacement for the camera’s `sdv` user-interface application. Lelouch reuses proprietary libraries and services recovered from the target firmware, so it is a replacement application for one researched board rather than a clean standalone firmware distribution. The repository explicitly notes that some included firmware, recovered libraries, and other components are proprietary or third-party.
projects.strategy: Reverse-engineer firmware containers and proprietary interfaces, then rebuild the `sdv` application interface against services and libraries already on the specific camera firmware.
projects.subtype: Action-camera application and firmware reverse engineering
projects.source_available: Public source repository and v0.0.1 release; no repository-wide license is declared in GitHub metadata. README says the tree contains recovered proprietary/third-party firmware material; it explicitly cautions that these components are not made open source by their presence.

projects.platform: VEX V5 ARM firmware and 32-bit ARM EABI user runtime; repository identifies VEXos 1.1.2.0 build 20220922.10.00.00 as its firmware snapshot.

projects.strategy: Inspect the VEX V5 runtime and extracted firmware, use symbols and disassembly to map the VEXos jump table, and reconstruct partial public/private API headers.
